findings: The straight tool view retains the source photograph's long socket, solid shaft, narrow red neck, flared finger stop, black bulbous grip and fixed red tail. No manufacturer logo is copied.

The socket end view exposes one aligned six-sided entrance and a real blind chamber. An initial differently clocked chamfer produced a star-shaped mouth; the builder was corrected and the current section test checks six-sided convex topology.
The grip end shows the rounded eight-edge profile and original 7 mm size text. The red tail is continuous with the hard molded core rather than a rotating precision-driver cap.
The assembled inspection preserves the original RS3 and clamp geometry and shows the complete tool in the selected engagement pose. The top close-up shows separation from the closure and band.

Source overall dimensions and the dual-material topology are supported. Exact contour, surface finish, internal retention, socket depth and clearance remain inferred; the model is not manufacturer CAD.

The catalogue's 36 mm maximum grip diameter is measured across radial corners, not its narrower flat-to-flat bounding box. The conflicting product-page socket diameters remain explicit; the larger alternative is included in the clearance envelope.
geometry_limits: Static complete-tool geometry and conservative rigid turning/withdrawal bounds do not establish hand grasp, worm motion, tightening torque or robot use.
The source product photographs and catalogue are external references only. The installed pose adds no inventory and is not an executed action.
